slides: Open by framing the chapter as the local-to-global integrability problem. A distribution gives allowed tangent directions, but the central question is whether those directions come from actual submanifolds. The notebook source span is printed pages 490-514 and the visual checks follow the bracket obstruction, Frobenius flat charts, foliations, Lie subgroups, and PDE compatibility.

Use the first example as the chapter's warning light. The two vector fields X equals partial x plus y partial z and Y equals partial y span a rank-two plane field, but their bracket is minus partial z. That direction is not in the span, so a surface trying to follow the plane field is forced to move in a missing direction.

Translate the same obstruction into the annihilator language. The 1-form alpha equals dz minus y dx cuts out the proposed distribution, and d alpha equals dx wedge dy. Evaluating d alpha on the spanning fields gives one, so the annihilator does not close under exterior differentiation.

Now show the positive model. Replacing Y by partial y plus x partial z makes the bracket vanish. The leaves are the surfaces z minus xy equals a constant, and the coordinate change u equals x, v equals y, w equals z minus xy has Jacobian determinant one, so the distribution is flattened to coordinate slices.

Move from local slices to global leaves. Frobenius says involutive distributions have local plaques, and maximal connected integral manifolds are obtained by gluing compatible plaques. The check records two connected components, each built from three local plaques across overlapping charts.

Connect the theorem to Lie theory. A Lie subalgebra gives a left-invariant involutive distribution on the Lie group, and the leaf through the identity is the connected Lie subgroup. On the torus, rational slope closes into a circle subgroup, while irrational slope gives an immersed nonclosed winding subgroup.

Show the PDE interpretation as another form of the same bracket test. A graph solution to u_x equals alpha and u_y equals beta must be tangent to two vector fields in the extended space. The compatible system has obstruction zero and solution u equals xy plus c; the incompatible system has obstruction one.

Use this lab slide to make students operate the theorem. The non-involutive example becomes integrable when the missing x partial z term is added to Y. A plotted surface can be visually tempting, but the bracket or 1-form test decides whether it is a genuine local integral manifold.

Summarize the theorem as a checklist: define the distribution, choose local spanning fields, test closure under Lie brackets or annihilating forms, then read off flat charts and leaves. The global theorem turns the local plaques into a foliation and explains the Lie subgroup and PDE applications.

Close with the chapter's through-line. Visual leaves are trustworthy only after the symbolic obstruction vanishes. When it vanishes, Frobenius produces flat coordinates, the leaves partition the manifold, Lie subalgebras integrate to connected subgroups, and overdetermined PDE systems gain local solutions.
